editorial.headline: Wood, Rattan, and Bamboo Tableware Meets Bali’s PMA Stop Line
editorial.standfirst: Nationally open to full foreign ownership, this craft-manufacturing activity is still blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the record’s risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the making of kitchenware and tableware whose main materials are wood, bamboo, and rattan. The record’s scope is practical and domestic: graters, spatulas, ladles, rice scoops, pestles and mortars, chopping boards, spoons, forks, chopsticks, glasses, plates, bowls, trays, lunch boxes, steamers, baskets, mats, toothpicks, and similar items. It is a manufacturing code for objects that sit close to everyday food culture, not a general furniture, craft-retail, or hospitality activity. Its centre of gravity is production: turning those natural materials into utensils and serving pieces intended for cooking, eating, carrying, or presenting food.

The registration picture is broad at the business-scale level. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, which means the code is not framed only for household workshops or only for industrial operators. A small bamboo utensil maker and a larger tableware producer can both sit within the same defined activity, provided the business being registered is genuinely the manufacture of the listed kitchen and dining goods. That breadth matters because the scope itself is material-specific and product-specific: the unifying point is not brand style or sales channel, but the making of kitchen and eating implements from wood, rattan, and bamboo.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clean. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national layer treats this activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no ownership cap below full foreign ownership in the slim record, and there is no additional national qualification stated here. For a founder reading only the national investment layer, this looks straightforward: the activity is open, the ceiling is full foreign ownership, and the source is explicitly named.

Bali changes the answer. The record marks l4_bali_blocked as true and gives the Bali status as Blocked (risk class). The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, which is blocked by the Bali moratorium dated May 13, 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is broader still: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source identified as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. So the honest conclusion is narrow but decisive: this activity may be nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, yet a foreign-owned company cannot register it in Bali today under the Bali-side block recorded here.
